message.content: I reviewed the saved notes (from 2024-11-04: long-term holder, large-cap tech preference, dividends reinvested manually), the account ($50,000 cash, 100 shares of MSFT, no notes restricting further purchases), and a live quote for AAPL ($222.70 last, $222.68 bid / $222.72 ask). AAPL fits the stated preference for large-cap technology and the mandate permits buy-only orders on AAPL up to $10,000 each and $20,000 total today, so I placed a single buy limit order for 40 shares at $222.75 — a limit essentially at the current ask, i.e., close to the market price — which filled at $222.75 for a total of $8,910, well within both the per-order and daily caps and leaving roughly $41,090 in cash with no money moved out of the account. The decision to add AAPL rested on the figures it reported in its FY2024 10-K filed 2024-11-01: revenue of $391.035 billion, net income of $93.736 billion, diluted EPS of $6.08, and operating cash flow of $118.254 billion — consistent, highly cash-generative results that support holding a large-cap tech position for the long term, at a price of about 36.6× trailing diluted EPS.
